'''Mbara''' (also known as '''Midjamba''', '''Mitjamba''', '''Ambara''', '''Balgalu''', or '''Bargal'''), and '''Yanga''' (also known as '''Jangaa''', '''Janggal''', '''Janga''', '''Yangaa''', '''Purkaburra''') are [[mutually intelligible]] but separate [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Aboriginal language]] of [[Queensland]], both now [[language extinction|extinct]].<ref name=aiatsisyanga>{{cite web |title=Y131: Yanga |work=Australian Indigenous Languages Database |publisher=[[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]] |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/Y131 |access-date=25 November 2020}}</ref><ref>RMW Dixon (2002), ''Australian Languages: Their Nature and Development'', p xxxii</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=G21: Mbara |work=Australian Indigenous Languages Database |publisher=[[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]] |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/G21 |access-date=25 November 2020}}</ref> [[Glottolog]] assigns a code to a group level as '''Mbara-Yanga''' (mbar1254). Yanga is not to be confused with the [[Yangga language]], a dialect of Biri.

The Mbara and Yanga people were traditionally neighbours, along with the [[Gugu-Badhun]], [[Yirandali]], [[Wunumara]] and [[Ngawun]] peoples. The expansion of cattle farming and [[Australian gold rushes|gold rushes]] in the second half of the nineteenth century affected the habitat of these groups.<ref name="ebscohost.com">{{cite book|url=http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/reference-entries/28811400/mbara|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107042023/http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/reference-entries/28811400/mbara|url-status=dead|archive-date=2015-01-07| chapter=Mbara| author=Horton, David R.|author-link=David Horton (writer)|date= Jan 1994|via=Ebsco Host Connection|title=Encyclopaedia of Aboriginal Australia: Vol. 2|page=674 |access-date=17 Oct 2020}}</ref>

According to [[AUSTLANG]], Yanga may be the same as [[Nyangga language]] and [[Ganggalida language|Ganggalida]].<ref name=aiatsisyanga/>
